# Backlog — planned improvements

## Commessa PDF generated by us (replace NetPro Crystal report)

*Noted 2026-10-06.*

**Today:** the print button (`/api/reports/commessa`) asks NetPro's report service (`192.168.1.91/SFCClient/Attachment/getPDFReport`) to run the Crystal report `BSORGCOMM2_NP.RPT`. That takes about 4.4 s per report (Crystal rendering), and since 2026-10 it needs a NetPro login (`NETPRO_WEB_USER` / `NETPRO_WEB_PASSWORD` in `.env.local`, see `src/lib/netproSession.ts`).

**Plan:** rebuild the same report in the app:
- **Data:** all fields come from the **Business DB**, read live.
- **Rendering:** server-side PDF (puppeteer, already installed), shown in the browser as a blob or inline. Merge editions directly.
- **Expected result:** about 0.3–1 s instead of about 4.4 s. No NetPro login needed and no dependency on NetPro's report service.

**Maintenance:** we maintain both NetPro reports ourselves. Whenever we change `BSORGCOMM2_NP.RPT` (or the other commessa report), change the in-app version too.

**Steps when we do it:**
1. Get `BSORGCOMM2_NP.RPT` from the NetPro server and read its queries, fields and layout (Crystal Designer or RptToXml).
2. Map each field to Business tables (commessa, client, article, phases/notes, materials, editions).
3. Build an HTML template, render it to PDF, and compare it side by side with the NetPro PDF for a few real orders (single and multi-edition).
4. Switch the print buttons over. Keep the NetPro route as a fallback until the new PDF is approved.

## Toolbar for writing Markdown (Agenda procedures and notes)

*Noted 2026-10-28.*

**Today:** `MarkdownField` is a text box with a preview; the symbols (`**bold**`, `- item`) are typed by hand.

**Plan:** a row of buttons above the box, built once inside `MarkdownField` so procedures, task notes and comments all get it:
- Bold, italic, heading, bullet list, numbered list, checklist, link: they wrap the selected text (or put the symbols at the cursor) and a second click takes them off.
- A **"?"** button opening a short cheat sheet popup (about ten lines of examples).
- No keyboard shortcuts for now (Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I can be added on top later).
- Tables and `- [ ]` checklists already show in the preview and wherever the text is displayed (`remark-gfm` in
  `src/components/ui/Markdown.tsx`): the toolbar only has to type them.

## Skins: a whole new look from one file

*Noted 2026-11-12; the groundwork was done on 2026-11-12 and 13.*

**Goal (owner):** restyle everything, in every part, by writing one file: a pixel / block-game look one day, a liquid
glass look another, with their own textures, borders, animations, fonts and icons. And few kinds of everything: what is
similar is one part, not two that differ a little.

**Done** (how it works is in the README → Design system):
- `theme.js` → `SKIN`: every corner size, the pace and curve of every transition, the animation of what opens over the
  page and of a press (both off), a picture behind the page; "reduce motion" on the computer is respected.
- One part for each thing a screen is made of, each drawn in one file of `src/components/ui/`: `Surface` (six kinds,
  tones, the selected look) and `Panel`; `Pressable` under `Button`, `IconButton`, `ChoiceButton`, tabs and switches;
  `FIELD` for every field; the `Table` parts for every table; `titleClasses` for every heading; `StatusBadge` for every
  label; `IconTile`; the one list of icons. `Card`, `Section`, `FormCard`, `TagCell`, the outlined button and the
  "soft" box are gone: each was a second way to draw something.
- Everything one presses is a shared kind, nothing is drawn by hand any more: `Button`, `IconButton`, `ChoiceButton`
  (the lights of Gruppi too), `SurfaceButton` (a box one presses), `MenuRow` (a row), `TextButton` (a word), `FoldToggle`
  and `FoldArrow` (what unfolds in place, one arrow everywhere). A link or a label that is pressed takes the same look
  from the part's classes (`pressableSurfaceClasses`, `menuRowClasses`): the cards of Gruppi and of the home pages, the
  pages of the sidebar, the table list of Esplora Database.
- The small grey label has one look: `titleClasses('label')` over a few lines, `FIELD_LABEL` (the same, on its own
  line) over a field, in `Field`, `Input` and `Select`. No screen writes it any more.
- A link read as text has three looks, in one file (`linkClasses`: accent, name, quiet); a value one presses in a
  table cell one (`VALUE_PRESSABLE`); a dashed box for what is not there yet one (`SURFACE_PENDING`). A table row that does
  not light up under the mouse says `still`; no screen switches a hover off by hand.
- What sits over what is eight named layers (`theme.js` → `LAYERS`: `z-raised` … `z-notice`); Tailwind's own numbers are
  switched off and the lint refuses one. A message of the app is now always on top.
- Sizes that are not a step of the scale are named in `theme.js` → `LAYOUT`; the lint refuses a size typed in a class
  and a class list glued with a template string. A bar that fills is `Meter`: five were drawn by hand, each with a
  style of its own. The only inline styles left outside the shared parts set a layout worked out while the page runs
  (the rows of the month, the columns of the week, the small bars of the coming weeks).
- What unfolds in place is one part, `Fold` (the pages of an area in the sidebar, a group of Da fare, a group of a
  settings table, the done cards of a day, a day of Le mie ore, the summary of a report, the filters on a phone): a
  skin animates all of them with `SKIN.motion.unfold`. It is 0s today, so they open at once as before. The rows of a
  table (Gruppi, Flusso Monetario, a row's details) unfold at once whatever the skin.
- ESLint refuses a fixed corner or pace, a hand-made box, a background of its own on a Surface, a raw `<button>`,
  `Pressable` outside the shared parts, an icon imported from the icon package; and, outside the shared parts, a look
  under the mouse, a cursor, a dashed edge and a title look written in a screen. A Claude Code session gets the
  errors of a file right after it edits it (`.claude/settings.json` → `scripts/lint-edited.js`).

**How the rules are kept, and what is still weak** (2026-11-13):
- The lint is a list of what is refused: a new way of drawing by hand passes until a rule names it. Stronger: a screen
  may write only spacing and layout, with a count of the places that still write more (about 237) that may only go down.
- The check before a push is `gitsync.bat` on this PC: a plain `git push` skips it. Stronger: the full check on GitHub
  for every push (to see first: the build downloads two fonts and may need what is only in `.env.local`).
- The check after an edit covers Claude Code sessions in this folder, and only files changed with Edit or Write: a
  file changed by a script or by hand waits for the lint of the whole project.
- No tool sees the screen: the page of every shared part (below), with screenshots compared automatically.
- A rule can be switched off with a comment (three today): a reason required for each, and a count.
- Texts and numbers typed in a screen are not checked by any tool.

**Still to do**, in this order:
1. **The floor plan** has one hand-made box; ESLint lets that folder off until it is next worked on.
2. **The switch and the proof**: the skin choice beside light / dark (`<html data-skin="…">`, a cookie), a page that
   shows every shared part side by side (superadmin, Strumenti), and one real second skin built from one file plus its
   images and font. It will need tokens that only make sense with it: the border width and style of a surface, a
   texture or a blur, a font for titles (in `titleClasses`), its own drawings for the icon names (in `icons.ts`), its
   `@keyframes`. Its selector must not outrank the reduce-motion rule. What still needs a hand there is the list of
   what the steps above missed.

**Not part of it:** the printed PDFs (their own colours, `src/lib/pdf/theme.ts`), Excel exports, what the app does.
**Limit:** dense tables of numbers stay readable only with a plain number font and calm effects; a skin keeps its show
for titles, panels and buttons (owner's choice, 2026-11-12).
**Not seen on screen yet:** all of the above was checked by types, lint and by comparing class lists, not by eye. The
merges changed the look in small ways (one transparency, one grey button, one selected look, four title sizes, tinted
options instead of filled ones): the first look at the pages after it may ask for a few values to be tuned, each in its
one place.
